title: GRPC: Fix the bug of GRPC-WEB decompression failure over HTTP1.1
description:
## Bug description:

If the message of grpc-web over http1.1 is compressed, the compression method will shipped with "grpc-encoding" http header in http request or http response package.

If we don't get "grpc-encoding" http header value while messages are sending in grpc-web over http1.1, the entity was not able to be decompressed like:
![unable-to-decompress](/uploads/fc3fde8b5730784b2649df182097054b/unable-to-decompress.jpg)

If this bug is fixed, the message will be decompressed correctly like:
![able-to-decompress](/uploads/b593acf271534e9c0a8ce0cc53178a85/able-to-decompress.jpg)

## Changes:

1. Passing header name/value map to sub-dissector in packet-http.c.
   Headers can also be used by dissectors other than grpc in the future.

2. Try to get the grpc-encoding header value in packet-grpc.c.
   This header contains decompression algorithm.

## Capture samples:
[client-grpc-web-text-http1-need-reassemble-gzip.pcapng](/uploads/96914719dabffaa19169ea447b60a625/client-grpc-web-text-http1-need-reassemble-gzip.pcapng)

The table above already has entries for other built in dissectors; there are entries for headers use by Websocket and HTTP2, for example. You should add the GRPC specific header to that table rather than creating another table, as that would be simpler.

changed this line in [version 8 of the diff](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/7362/diffs?diff_id=443685169&start_sha=2595127d5c0a756f1dde5d8f04006b3b18f93d5e#91141fe8031a8b6c0d94c5cbea195c97ee2bdc4d_2872_2871)

This is a little brittle because it finds the first match in the tree, and if the frame has multiple HTTP messages with different GRPC encodings odd things can happen.

A rare case, perhaps, but if that can happen the Right Thing is to retrieve the header value from the HTTP message, such as by adding it to the HTTP message info (since as I understand it this is a per message not per conversation variable.)
